**Prime status comes from the account itself, and the HWID spoofer can give an account fresh identifiers on every launch.**

## New

- **New profile every launch.** Settings > HWID spoofer. Each launch of a spoofed account gets newly generated hardware identifiers instead of the profile it kept from its first spoofed launch. Off by default. (#4)
- **A new account can get its HWID profile before its first sign-in.** With Spoof every launch on, an account that had never launched offered only "Exclude from spoofing" in its HWID spoofer menu, and got its profile when it first signed in. The menu now has "Generate a profile" for it, so you can create or replace the profile ahead of time.

## Fixed

- **Prime status is no longer guessed.** The app used to estimate Prime from the CS2 level and XP, so an account with XP but no Prime showed as Prime. Steam tells only the account itself whether it has Prime, so the status is now read from the account's own CS2 Game Coordinator data once it has connected: open it on the CS2 screen, and token-only accounts are checked on refresh. Until then the Accounts screen says "Likely Prime" or "Unknown" and tells you how to check. (#3)
- **An expired competitive cooldown no longer shows as one lasting decades.** The Game Coordinator sends the time left as a signed number, and a cooldown that had already run out was read as one ending 68 to 136 years from now. Stored values like that are cleared when the vault opens.
- **Settings say where Prime comes from.** The GCPD scraper reads ranks, CS2 level and cooldown, not Prime.

## Notes

- Accounts keep their stored Prime value as an estimate until they connect to the Game Coordinator once, so some show "Likely Prime" after the update.
- Nothing else in the vault changes. Accounts, vaults, master passwords and settings carry over.

<details>
<summary><b>Requirements and first run</b></summary>

**Requirements.** Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Statically linked, so no Visual C++ redistributable.

**First run.** The binary is unsigned, so SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. Code-signing certificates are not free.

**Upgrading.** Replace the exe and start it.

**Privacy.** No telemetry. The app talks to Steam for the features you use, and to GitHub only if you enable the update check.

</details>
